<explanation>
Based on the file tree and the README, the project “biliLive-tools” is clearly a monorepo organizing a suite of tools for managing live streams – from recording (supporting multiple platforms like Bilibili, DouYu, HuYa, DouYin), converting and compressing videos with danmu (live comment) integration, to offering both a desktop application (built with Electron) and command-line interfaces. It’s also designed to run as a web server/API (with Dockerized containers for “api” and “webui”) and includes robust webhook support for automated processing. Here’s how you can draw an accurate system design diagram that reflects its architecture:

1. Identify and Label the Main Components:
   • Monorepo Core: Show that the project is managed as a monorepo using a PNPM workspace (indicated by “pnpm-lock.yaml” and “pnpm-workspace.yaml”).
   • Recording Libraries: Separate packages (e.g., BilibiliRecorder, DouYinRecorder, DouYuRecorder, HuYaRecorder, and also huya-danmu) function as the core modules for handling platform-specific recording, danmu processing, and stream management.
   • CLI Module: The “CLI” package encapsulates the command-line interface functionalities.
   • Desktop Application: The “app” package is clearly the Electron-based desktop client. Inside it you have split responsibilities (main process, renderer process) for handling application logic and UI components.
   • HTTP/API Service: The “http” package defines middleware, routes, and services to accept webhook calls and API requests.
   • Shared/Common Utilities: The “shared” and “types” packages include common code (utilities, database models, presets, configuration) used across modules.
   • Live Manager & Others: The “liveManager” package further orchestrates live stream recording and processing.
   • Docker & Deployment Components: The “docker” folder (and associated GitHub workflows) indicates containerized versions of the backend API, web UI, and third-party recorder integration (e.g., BililiveRecorder/recorder).

2. Outline the Relationships and Interactions:
   • Show that the Desktop App (Electron UI) and the CLI interact with the underlying recording libraries and shared utilities.
   • The HTTP/API service (backend) exposes routes such as webhook endpoints (e.g., for BililiveRecorder, blrec, DDTV, custom webhooks) that trigger processing in the recording modules.
   • The Docker deployment section encapsulates the “api” and “webui” containers – the diagram should show these as separate containers, with directional arrows representing network communication (API calls, webhook callbacks).
   • The Shared package is used by multiple components (CLI, HTTP API, Live Manager, Desktop App) to maintain consistency in presets, configuration, and type definitions.

3. Emphasize Architectural Patterns and Design Principles:
   • Modular Design: Clearly illustrate each package/module as an independent component within the monorepo while noting their reusability (like shared utilities and types).
   • Separation of Concerns: Distinguish between the UI layers (Desktop App, WebUI), service layers (HTTP/mock API service), and core domain libraries (recorders, live management).
   • Microservices Components (in Docker): Note the separation between the “frontend” container (web UI) and “backend” container (API server) in a Docker Compose environment.
   • Extensibility: Indicate that the design supports plugin-like recording modules for platforms, making it easy to add more in the future.

4. Detail the Technologies, Frameworks, or Libraries Involved:
   • Electron is used for the desktop application (packages/app).
   • Likely Vue (or a similar framework) is used in the renderer process for building the UI (as seen from the “src/renderer” structure and .vue components).
   • Node.js is the runtime environment (with a defined .node-version).
   • Tools like ffmpeg, DanmakuFactory, and possibly better-sqlite3 (for danmu analysis) are integrated as binary dependencies.
   • Docker is used for containerized deployments, and GitHub Actions streamline CI/CD.

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram to This Project:
   • Separate the diagram into layers:
       - The Presentation/UI Layer: Illustrate the Desktop app (Electron) and WebUI (docker container) with clear arrows to the API.
       - The Application/Service Layer: Depict the HTTP API service, the CLI entry point, and live management modules.
       - The Data/Processing Layer: Include the platform-specific recorders (Bilibili, DouYin, etc.) and shared utilities.
       - The Deployment Layer: Illustrate Docker components, volumes (for data persistence like “video”, “data”, “fonts”), and external integrations (webhook endpoints, SMTP, server酱, etc.).
   • Use clear labels for every module (e.g., “Electron App (GUI)”, “CLI”, “HTTP Service (API & Webhooks)”, “BilibiliRecorder Module”, “Shared Utils & Types”, “LiveManager”).
   • Draw directional arrows to indicate data flow (for example, how webhook events flow from external sources into the HTTP service, then trigger recording modules; how commands from the CLI or Desktop App invoke shared libraries).
   • Color-code or use different shapes to distinguish between UI components, backend services, external integrations, and shared libraries.

6. Detailed Instructions for Creating the Diagram:
   • Start by sketching boxes for each top-level component:
         - Monorepo Container (PNPM Workspace) encompassing all packages.
         - Inside the container, place sub-boxes for “Desktop App (Electron)”, “CLI”, “HTTP/API Service”, “Recording Libraries (Bilibili, DouYin, DouYu, HuYa)”, “LiveManager”, and “Shared Utilities/Types”.
         - Off to one side, illustrate the Docker components (“backend” API container, “webui” container, recorder container) with configuration details like mapped volumes and environment variables.
   • Draw arrows:
         - From “Web UI” to “HTTP/API Service” (indicating REST API interactions).
         - From “HTTP/API Service” to each “Recording Library”, showing that API calls trigger recording, conversion, compression, and webhook events.
         - From “Desktop App” and “CLI” to “Shared Utilities” and “Recording Libraries”, highlighting a common dependency.
         - From external webhook sources (like BililiveRecorder’s webhook) into the “HTTP/API Service”.
   • Label everything clearly and consider using legends (for color codes or shapes) to represent different types of components – for example:
         - Rectangles for applications (CLI, Desktop App),
         - Cylinders for databases (if applicable in shared/db models),
         - Cloud icons for external services (SMTP, server酱, etc.),
         - Rounded rectangles for Docker containers.
   • Include any important configuration aspects such as volume mappings (e.g., “./data”, “./video”, “./fonts”) between the host and container that are critical for persistence.

By following these instructions and emphasizing each component’s role and its interactions with others, you’ll have a detailed system design diagram that truly represents the architecture of “biliLive-tools”. Make sure to include all key elements (modules, interactions, dependencies, external services) and use directional arrows, clear labels, and visual differentiation (colors or shapes) as described.
</explanation>
